# `s(69)` — open

Open. The best known packing gives `s(69) ≤ 8.82721206`, and the best proved lower bound
is `8.348469` from Nagamochi’s general theorem, leaving a gap of `0.4787`. General
closed form: s(N) >= min(ceil(sqrt(N)), sqrt(N - 2*floor(sqrt(N)) + 1) + 1).

## The packing

Found by Maurizio Morandi in 2010, via a hand construction.
Later improved by David W. Cantrell.
Its side length is algebraic of degree **82** over `ℚ`.

## The lower bound

Nothing specific to this `n` has ever been proved.
The bound is Nagamochi’s general closed form, which applies to every `N ≥ 4`:

```
s(N) ≥ min{ ⌈√N⌉,  √(N − 2⌊√N⌋ + 1) + 1 }
```

This is the default across almost the whole open frontier — 63 of the 65 open cases at
`n ≤ 100` are governed by it, and it has not been improved since 2005.
